Method of Attack: Creating malicious .RAR and .ZIP archives that display seemingly innocuous files (e.g., JPG, PDF, TXT) but execute scripts upon opening to install malware
Exploitation of WinRAR zero-day vulnerability CVE-2023-38831 to launch CMD scripts that install malware
Launching self-extracting (SFX) CAB archives to infect devices
Remote access trojan capabilities including arbitrary command execution, keylogging, screen capturing, file management, and reverse proxy
Impacted Systems: Windows devices infected via malicious archives
Attack Vector: Maliciously crafted WinRAR ZIP or RAR archives distributed on cryptocurrency and stock trading forums
Double-clicking on decoy files (PDFs, images, text files) inside archives triggers malware installation
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious archives containing CMD scripts executed via CVE-2023-38831
Malware families DarkMe, GuLoader, Remcos RAT infections
Forum posts with links to malicious archives targeting crypto traders
WinRAR version 6.23 patch released August 2, 2023 fixing CVE-2023-38831 and CVE-2023-40477
